articles.summary: The Manatee Motel is a Kingfishers Illegal Operation in Grand Theft Auto VI. It contains two Key Valuables to find, including cash and a unique weapon variant.
articles.body:
The Manatee Motel is a Kingfishers Illegal Operation in Grand Theft Auto VI . It contains two Key Valuables to find, including cash and a unique weapon variant. This official IGN GTA 6 guide teaches you how to find every Key Valuable at the Manatee Motel, and points out optional items and extra cash so you’re coming away with a great payout.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

The Kingfishers Manatee Motel Illegal Operation is located northeast of Cottonmouth Lake and south of Hamlet in Mariana County . It first becomes available in Chapter 2. It’s an open area with no specific entrance, so feel free to enter the area from whatever direction you’d like.

As Illegal Operations go, this is a smaller one, meaning less enemies to fight. That said, don’t underestimate the fights here; the Kingfishers can call in reinforcements in vehicles and it can get out of hand fast. On the plus side, there’s plenty of cover to hide behind.

Watch out for the loose dog roaming around as it can deal a lot of damage if it sics you. If it does, mash Square / Y to push it off you.

There are two Key Valuables to find in the Manatee Motel Illegal Operation. Click on a link below to jump to that specific one for more information:

The first Key Valuable is a safe, located inside the main motel building, directly in the middle . Look for the brown graffiti that reads “SPEED LIVE” – the motel room you need is to the right.

Enter the room but be careful! There may be a tiger in here. If there is, it might be distracted and chomping down on someone – if so, use this opportunity to take it out before it spots you.

Walk to the back of the room to find a small safe on top of a shelf. You don’t need a code for this one; simply press Triangle / X and then find the sweet spot with Right Stick to bust it open with a screwdriver. Inside, there’s $937 in cash.

Before you move on, look on the left side of the room, where there are animal cages. There’s an Adrenaline on top, as well as a first aid kit with a second Adrenaline inside.

Directly opposite the animal cages, look on the small table to find a money-counting machine with several stacks of cash totaling $484 . There’s also a pack of cigarettes on the arm of the couch to the left.

The second and final Key Valuable is located inside the main motel building, in a room to the left of the same brown “SPEED LIVE” graffiti from the first Key Valuable.

Go inside the room and look in the right back corner to find the Kingfishers Laird 350 Sniper unique weapon variant.

Picking it up will complete the Kingfisher Manatee Motel Illegal Operation, but there are still some items to find, if you’d like.

While in the same room as the Kingfishers Laird 350 Sniper unique weapon variant, look on the table on the left side to find two cocaine bricks that you can sell to a fence and $342 in cash.

On the other side of the room, there is a crate of Molotov cocktails and a pack of Macizo cigars .

Don’t forget to loot any downed Kingfisher enemies, too! They can carry additional cash, healing items, and drugs, boosting your score further.

articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) appears to be heading towards a record-breaking launch, with early sales estimates pointing to strong demand across PlayStation and Xbox consoles. According to Sensor Tower's sales tracker, last updated on November 18, 2026, the game has sold an estimated 17.07 million units and generated $1.65 billion in revenue, net of returns. These figures suggest that GTA 6 has crossed the $1 billion revenue mark within a short period, with sales continuing to increase.The estimates also show that PlayStation accounts for the majority of sales. Around 75% of the estimated copies sold were for PlayStation, while Xbox accounted for the remaining 25%.GTA 6 pre-orders reportedly exceed expectationsWhile Rockstar Games has not released official pre-order figures, its parent company Take-Two Interactive has indicated that demand is stronger than expected. In its latest earnings report, Take-Two said GTA 6 pre-orders were "tracking far above our initial expectations". The company has not shared exact numbers, so Sensor Tower's figures offer an estimate of the game's early sales performance.A latest report by Reuters said that the analysts at Wells Fargo estimate GTA 6 to sell nearly 65 million units by March 2027 – an increase of 30 million from the previous estimate of 35 million sales.How GTA 6 sales are split between PlayStation and XboxSensor Tower's tracker shows a clear lead for PlayStation in the platform-wise sales mix. articles.title: Sunrise RV Park - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Sunrise RV Park is an Illegal Operation in Grand Theft Auto VI, ran by the Kingfishers gang. It's home to three Key Valuables, including cash and a
articles.body:
The Sunrise RV Park is an Illegal Operation in Grand Theft Auto VI , ran by the Kingfishers gang. It's home to three Key Valuables, including cash and a unique weapon variant. This official IGN GTA 6 guide teaches you how to find every Key Valuable in the Kingfishers Sunrise RV Park Illegal Operation and points out extra items and cash along the way so you can come away with full pockets and a heavy wallet.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

The Kingfishers Sunrise RV Park Illegal Operation is located northwest of Key Lento, on the north side of Cottonmouth Lake . While you can take any approach to get there, such as by boat, the easiest way by vehicle is to take the road that leads southwest out of Hamlet until you reach the front gate, as shown in our map screenshot below. But, again, there’s no definitive entrance you must use .

A shotgun is particularly useful here because of how many Kingfisher enemies are in close proximity to each other. If you don’t have one, there’s at least one Kingfisher in the camp that has one you can take by force – lethally or otherwise. You may also find one just laying around.

Additionally, watch out for dogs as you loot the Sunrise RV Park. They can be particularly nasty and they’re fast, meaning one can just spring out on you from nowhere.

There are three Key Valuables inside Sunrise RV Park, all closely guarded by Kingfishers. Click on a Key Valuable below to jump to more information on obtaining it:

The first Key Valuable is a safe located inside the main Sunrise RV office building, near the center of the compound . If you’re coming in from the main gate, it’s the first building you’ll see on your left.

Inside, look behind the front desk to find the safe.

There’s a Zombix you can grab on the front desk here, just in front of the TV. Additionally, there’s a first aid cabinet on the wall to the left of the safe. Open it to find a first aid kit containing an Adrenaline .

You don’t need a code for this safe . Simply press Triangle / X to get out your screwdriver, then use Right Stick to find the sweet spot and it’ll pop open.

Inside, you’ll find $1,332 in cash. Nice!

Look just to the right of the first safe inside the office building to find a table with a Zombix and a notepad. Interact with the notepad to find the safe code for the second safe: Tap to Reveal .

You’ll need this if you don’t have access to Sticky Bombs, which you unlock Tap to Reveal .

The second Key Valuable is a safe located inside the big building on the dock in the south section of the Sunrise RV Park .

There’s a first aid box on the wall to the right of the door. Open it to find an Adrenaline and a Zombix .

Head inside and the safe will be just ahead of you in the back, next to a yellow “LIVE BAIT & TACKLE” sign.

If you have Sticky Bombs unlocked, go ahead and plant one on the safe to blow the door open. But if not, you’ll need the safe code. If you missed it earlier, it’s on a table directly to the right of the first safe inside the main office building. Or, if you don’t want to go back for it, the safe code is: Tap to Reveal .

Inside, you’ll find cash on the top shelf ( $1,590 ) and more cash on the second shelf ( $669 ), totaling $2,259 .

Before you leave to find the final Key Valuable, check the tables in this building to find several cocaine bricks , $228 in cash, and a packet of cigarettes .

The third and final Key Valuable is located inside an orange and white RV in the south section of the Sunrise RV Park , just north of the dock.

Go inside the door on the left and you’ll see the Kingfishers Akulus Revolver unique weapon variant on the bed, which is the Key Valuable. If you’re entering from the other door, just walk left and you’ll reach the bedroom.

There’s more to loot in this RV, though, so don’t leave just yet!

Look on the table to the left of the weapon case the Kingfishers Akulus Revolver was in to find $57 cash.

Walk through the RV into the bathroom and you’ll see a small safe on the counter next to the sink.

Leave the RV and immediately look ahead of you for a white building with a big hole in the side of it.

Inside, you’ll find another first aid kit on a table if you need more healing items, $219 on the workbench to the left, and another pack of cigarettes .

Make sure to loot any downed Kingfishers you may have missed on your way out, as they can be carrying extra cash. And don’t forget to visit a fence to offload the cocaine bricks!

Who you sell the drugs to will vary, but if you’re in Chapter 2 when the Sunrise RV Park first becomes available, Tap to Reveal will pay $2,400 for them.

articles.title: A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms Season 1 4K Blu-rays Drop to a New Low Price at Amazon
articles.body:
The Amazon Black Friday deals are now live , where you can save on dozens of physical media items like video games, movies, board games, and seasons of great TV shows. One of these is the 4K Blu-ray version of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms season 1, which is marked down to $22.99 from its original list price of $34.99.

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms Season 1 4K Blu-ray

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms was 2026's first foray back into George R.R. Martin's fantasy world of Westeros. Based on the first of three prequel short stories also known as Tales of Dunk and Egg, HBO's show is an engaging and more comedically-toned version of their Game of Thrones world. There's still plenty of political and royal intrigue, violent action, and great world building, but it's a more standalone show compared to Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon .

We gave season one an 8 out of 10 in our review , saying it "may not have dragons, but A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms has plenty of heart, charm and humor -- and two endearing lead performances -- that make this a more than worthy watch". Season 2 is on the way, and we've learned a little more about what to expect .

Like all HBO shows, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms is available to stream in 4K with an HBO Max Premium subscription , but the picture quality you get from that just isn't going to be nearly as good as what you get with Blu-ray discs. This is largely because streaming services offer lower bitrates compared to 4K Blu-rays . A higher bitrate means a more detailed picture.

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (Tales of Dunk and Egg) Book

If you're curious about catching up the source material and checking out the second and third short stories (which seasons 2 and 3 will likely follow), the paperback version of the book is also pretty cheap on Amazon right now. Pick one up for $12.34, down from its usual $20 price tag.

articles.title: Burger King Parodies GTA's Heart Stopper Burger With Real-Life, 7-Patty 'HeartWhopper'
articles.summary: Burger King parodies GTA 6 with ‘HeartWhopper’ burger featuring 7 stacked patties.
articles.body:
GTA 6 has officially launched in all time zones, and while Rockstar has been marketing its heart out for what feels like a lifetime, one fast-food chain waited until launch to join in on the fun.

Burger Shot, a parody of Burger King, has been a staple of the Grand Theft Auto series since the original Vice City game. Now, Burger King in Belgium is "taking back what they’re owed" by turning an iconic Burger Shot offering into a real-life product: the HeartWhopper.

The 'heart' of it all isn’t about how much Burger King loves GTA — it refers to how likely this thing is to give you a heart attack.

While Burger Shot first appeared in Vice City, the 'Heart Stopper' burger was a big part of the background world in GTA 4. In-game, you hear commercials for the burger with customers dialing 9-1-1 as they eat. The burger’s slogan? “Oh, I think my heart just stopped!”

Just like the super-sized in-game product, Burger King’s HeartWhopper features a whopping seven beef patties in addition to the usual lettuce, tomato, and onion slices.

It's worth noting you can't simply walk into a Burger King in Belgium and buy a HeartWhopper from the menu. Rather, you can win one through a two-week social media competition where you share a video clip of yourself eating a burger from the in-game restaurant and Burger King Belgium picks its favorite each day.

Burger King is launching a sizable marketing campaign for the new release, so don’t be shocked when the HeartWhopper pops up during whatever GTA 6 stream you’re watching. Local chains are having plenty of fun with the promotion, like Burger King Belgium sharing "We might get 6 stars for this."

The HeartWhopper has some competition, however. Rockstar is partnering with local Florida restaurant Skinny Louie to turn a selection of restaurants into real 'Burger Shot' locations over the next couple of months. Popeye’s is also dropping its own GTA 6 sandwich , and I’m sure meme-loving Wendy’s has something in the works.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

articles.title: 'Unprecedented. Unbelievable. Unmissable.' The 'GTA 6' reviews are in — here's what they're saying.
articles.summary: It's the first entry in the Rockstar Games franchise in over a decade, and critics are raving about the long-awaited return to Vice City.
articles.body:
The much-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here, and critics who have spent weeks playing it before the public say it's worth the hype.

The open-world format of GTA 6 allows gamers to explore Vice City , the sun-drenched fictional Miami-like metropolis in the Florida-like state of Leonida, as the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like criminal duo Jason and Lucia.

"Rockstar's Vice City is a masterpiece I never want to leave," PC Mag's Jordan Minor wrote in his review . " Grand Theft Auto VI is simply one of the best-looking video games I've ever seen."

"Unprecedented. Unbelievable. Unmissable," declared IGN's Luke Reilly . "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played."

Same for the Guardian's Keza MacDonald , who gave it a glowing review .

"In GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen," MacDonald wrote, adding: "Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start."

Here's what other top gaming critics are saying about GTA VI.

This is a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work required to make them successful. The surprising depth to which these themes are explored makes for a memorable and endearing experience in Grand Theft Auto VI, which largely lives up to its sky-high expectations by inverting the series's reputation for destruction.

Not only do they have very different motivations than past GTA protagonists, wanting to create a better life for themselves and escape their life of crime instead of vying to become crime lords or get revenge, but they are easily Rockstar's most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters.

Through Jason and Lucia's genuine chemistry, GTA 6 gives you a better reason to work through Leonida's daily grind. Yes, there's always another bank to rob or car to steal, but that's not the reason you wake up in the morning. It's to prove that love can survive in a cruel culture that tries so hard to beat it out of people. So be it if you have to play dirty to keep pace with the cold-hearted crooks who make their fortune from someone else's pain. It shouldn't be this hard to settle down with your lover and enjoy a sunset together in the rotten social climate that Rockstar has been eager to lampoon for decades at this point. articles.title: GTA 6's Prologue Can Go Way More Differently Than You Might Think
articles.summary: GTA 6's prologue can go more way more differently than you might think.
articles.body:
Although it may seem like you’re being overwhelmed from all angles by the police after Lucia’s bungled robbery in GTA 6’s prologue, it is technically possible to evade them and make a clean getaway. That is, until GTA 6’s story immediately course-corrects and sends you back to the scene of the crime.

The first time I booted up GTA 6, I was quite overwhelmed by a combination of the dazzling visuals and the urgent need to retrain my brain to click the left stick to sprint rather than hammer the X button. As a result, although I still made a good fist of Lucia’s desperate escape – hustling down a street behind the coffee shop and Ferris Bueller-ing my way over a series of backyard fences – I was eventually brought down by a VCPD officer’s taser bolt that hit me right between the shoulder blades. At this point, the cuffs were slapped onto Lucia’s wrists and the game flash-forwarded back to the present day where GTA 6’s co-protagonist continued her consultation with her correctional counselor in Leonida Penitentiary, and the story launched gloriously into the game’s first chapter.

I suspect that most players will have a similar experience during the opening moments of Rockstar’s latest crime epic. However, out of curiosity, I decided to start a fresh save and see if I could get the better of Vice City’s boys in blue. This time, after the annoying good samaritan wrestled Lucia to the floor and the clerk shuttered his window and triggered the alarm, I made a dash across the street and crashed through the gates of an abandoned lot under an overpass. With my Wanted level immediately at two stars and the shriek of sirens rapidly swelling in volume, I frantically scrambled around the edge of a building and… clumsily tripped and fell straight into a canal.

This soggy slip-up probably should have sealed my fate, but it actually proved to be my salvation, as I swam up to the surface and straddled a Seashark jet ski that was idly bobbing up and down next to a nearby dock. After briefly fumbling with the new twin-stick hotwiring mechanic I wrenched the throttle and tore off down the waterway, deftly swerving around a couple of fishing boats as the sirens faded into the background and the skyrises of Vice City’s downtown area loomed ahead of me. I was free.

Once again the story jumped back to the present, with the counselor asking the orange jumpsuit-wearing Lucia, “You rode a what?” to which Lucia replied, “A Seashark. I mean, it’s Vice City. Everyone’s got one.” This leads me to presume that voice actor Manni L. Perez recorded an alternate line naming literally every possible vehicle in the area that Lucia could have escaped in, because GTA 6 is insane like that and there’s a reason it takes up 200GB of your console’s hard drive space.

There’s also a reason that, despite the fact I managed to pierce through the police’s dragnet and find freedom, Lucia still ended up behind bars – and GTA 6 quickly addresses it. Reading her file, the counselor asks, “It says here you got away, but then you went back?” At this point the game once again flashes back to the day of the incident where Lucia, gym bag stuffed with stolen cash still slung around her shoulders, is making her way back to the scene of the crime (for crucial story reasons I won’t spoil here). My two-star Wanted level had changed to red, indicating that although I had lost the cops, they were familiar with my appearance and were still on the lookout for me.

However, there didn’t seem to be any officers in my vicinity, so I calmly walked in the direction of the coffee shop and tried not to draw any attention to myself. Before I had a chance to figure out exactly where that annoying beeping sound was coming from, the dye packet hidden in my bag of stolen cash suddenly exploded, splashing pink ink all over Lucia’s workout clothes and immediately alerting every cop in the area. Then came the sirens, then came the patrolmen spilling out from all the nearby sidestreets, then came the heartstopping jolt of a taser bolt as Lucia collapsed and spasmed facedown on the asphalt. The cuffs were once again snapped onto her wrists, and the story shifted back to the present to crash into GTA 6’s first chapter much like it had the first time around.

I’m yet to try a third time to try and find out what would have happened if I had managed to return to the coffee shop, or perhaps made a successful escape from the cops a second time, because I’m now neck deep in Jason’s smalltime crime capers and home renovations in the Leonida Keys area. But I just love that from the very first moments that you gain control over one of its characters, GTA 6 feels like it’s been designed to anticipate your every move and instinct and be able to roll with it no matter how the events play out. I can’t wait for the hundreds of hours of experimentation that lay ahead.

Christopher Ruocchio’s science-fiction epic, The Sun Eater, tells the harrowing tale of how the son of duke who dreamed of being an explorer and scholar would go on to destroy a star and an entire civilization. After having devoured the books earlier this year, the tale of Hadrian (who I lovingly explain to my friends is “what if Jesus was a Jedi”) and his Red Company quickly has become one of my favorite reads in a long time, putting it right up there with Pierce Brown’s Red Rising series .

articles.summary: GTA 6 sold around 20 million copies via preorders before the game's general release, analysts estimate.
articles.body:
GTA 6 sold around 20 million copies via preorders before the game's general release, analysts estimate.

Data published by Sensor Tower shows 17.07 million copies sold by November 16, with still a couple of days to go before launch. By that point, GTA 6's daily pre-order sales were averaging over a million per day, making the 20 million copy milestone a likely estimate for Rockstar's blockbuster — even before it officially went on sale.

Sensor Tower data suggests the game has already surpassed $1.6 billion in revenue, with 75% of sales for PlayStation 5 and just 25% on Xbox Series X/S.

While Rockstar is yet to release any official preorder or sales numbers itself, it seems that shareholders in its parent company, Take-Two, are happy. Take-Two's share price remains lower than its all-time high set around this time last year, during the midst of the GTA 6 hype cycle, but the company's stocks have risen steadily over the course of this month.

Yesterday's publication of reviews — which left GTA 6 as the joint-highest rated game of all time — helped drive this further, with shares rising 6% from a low of $203 on November 17 to a high of $222 when markets closed last night. And, of course, it likely won't be long before Take-Two reveals just how well GTA 6 has officially done. Any guesses?

Earlier this month, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick told IGN in an interview that he was feeling “optimistic” about the launch of GTA 6, with preorders tracking “far in excess” of the company’s initial expectations.

articles.title: The wait begins for GTA VI on PC
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X / S. While PC gamers are left out, there are many indicators that it’ll be worth the wait.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here for millions of players who own a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X / S, and those who plan to buy a console, despite rising costs this year, just to play it. As you have likely already noticed, the launch is inescapable, and that’s especially tough if you’re a PC gamer. I’m sorry to remind you that the clock has only just now started ticking down to the unannounced yet inevitable release of the PC version. Good luck with avoiding Twitch and browsing the internet while trying to remain oblivious to the violent (and romantic) delights that await you. Seeing Leonida in true 4K at an unlocked frame rate with full ray-tracing effects and extended draw distances, among other graphical improvements, might be a thing you can do on your PC as early as sometime in Q1 2027, if recent reports are accurate. Regardless, early 2027 is not right now. Speaking as someone with a capable gaming desktop, I’m sad to say that FOMO has already gotten the best of me. I bought GTA VI on the PS5 and will probably double-dip and buy it again on PC, just like I did with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2. The psychology of me, a weak-willed consumer, is one that publisher Rockstar Games and really any other company in its position would be happy to exploit. [Image: The PC version of GTA VI will launch, eventually, in a very different landscape than the PC ports of Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA V did. Despite the recent downturn in PC sales driven by increased RAM prices, there are considerably more players on PC now than there were a decade ago. SteamDB’s charts show that Steam’s concurrent users alone have more than doubled (from around 20 million to over 40 million now) since 2020. A chunk of those people are likely made up of console expats who decided to migrate to PC for various reasons. Some wanted to experience the fun of building their own desktop, while some were mainly convinced by the fact that you can get more power for your money with a PC than with a PlayStation 5 Pro or Xbox Series X. For a subset of people, the convenience of getting something like a Steam Deck to bring your PC game library with you anywhere more than makes up for its lack of power. There are many other justifiable reasons for making PC your main gaming platform, like getting faster access to discounts on digital games, not paying for online multiplayer, ultrawide monitor resolutions, being able to buy games from one of several platforms, and having one device that you can use for work and play. Rockstar seems poised to deliver the definitive version of GTA VI on PC on its own terms, and I’m interested to see what the end result will be. In addition to building the best-looking version of the game made to run well across countless configurations, its PC optimization efforts are likely also more focused than before on ensuring decent performance on lower-end hardware (including PC handhelds). With a 200-plus-gigabyte install size on consoles, I dread how big it’ll be on PC. Ideally, the PC version will launch alongside an improved version of GTA Online (whether it’s free to play is anyone’s guess), and maybe with upgraded GTA roleplay tech to support it. I’m hopeful that the PC version of GTA VI will come in early 2027, but if the numerous delays of the console versions were any indication, the developer will take all the time it needs to get it right. Update, 9:55AM ET, November 19th: The SteamDB data cited now specifies that it’s concurrent users, not the number of users total.

articles.title: GTA 6’s Opening Two Hours Teach You Everything You’ll Ever Need To Know About the Next 100
articles.summary: GTA 6 has a slower, more deliberate opening than previous GTA games, but it's the perfect introduction to this 100 hour adventure.
articles.body:
Warning: Spoilers for the first hour of GTA 6’s Chapter 1 follow.

GTA 6’s open world is one packed full of distractions.

After its short prologue and quick drug-running operation around the fictional Florida Keys, you wake up as Jason, ready to continue his crime-centered day job as a collections man for his boss, Brian. Three different main mission markers are then offered to you, ushering you into the familiar GTA rhythm you’ll likely spend much of the next 100 hours moving to. But the real beauty of what makes this game so special is the unpredictability of what happens in between those major moments, and the choices you make both in and out of missions.

GTA 6 lets you live Jason and Lucia’s lives how you wish, with small decisions and unforeseen distractions shaping its epic story and your place within its world. In just its first hour of setting you free, it puts all of these possibilities on display in subtle ways, drip-feeding its systems into your brain. It’s a menu of opportunity so dense it could easily feel overwhelming, but instead is introduced to you so smoothly it all becomes second nature. It’s a perfect slice of game design, and the best opening to a game that Rockstar has ever produced.

The first thing you’ll likely notice when stepping into this fictional Florida is just how ridiculously good it looks. Clothing textures, little quirks of animation, and phenomenal lighting tech draw you into its near-lifelike environments. That realism, and how each of its characters moves and acts like real people, instantly impacted the way I controlled Jason. I treated him as if he were an actual human being, rather than a video game avatar. It all starts with routine. I hopped out of bed, and instead of just running out of the door and to the first mission marker that caught my attention, I took my time, making sure to shower, get dressed, have a cup of coffee, and feed my pet snake, Dolores, before heading out.

That sensation of routine is something I not only found myself emulating throughout my first day in Leonida, but over the course of the whole story. I’d often do one or two missions and then head home, rather than going from one slice of action to the next without resting as I would in so many other open-world games. It’s something carried over from Red Dead Redemption 2’s masterful design, in which I’d treat Arthur in a very similar fashion — making sure to shave, bathe, and brew some coffee every day before embarking on a day of lawbreaking. Of course, Red Dead 2 doesn’t get to its simulation of daily life straight away, instead choosing to open with a slow, steady, and snowy opening that rewards patience. I’m a huge fan of how Rockstar’s Western begins, but I know that isn’t a universally shared opinion. GTA 6 gets you into the action much faster, though, and shows its hand early through its first string of quick-hit missions.

The first thing I decided to check off my list was visiting Ammu-Nation to pick up a new gun. After a friendly chat with the owner and a newly acquired shotgun slung across my shoulder, I found myself promptly putting it to use. Three gang members who were unhappy about me murdering a few of their friends in the opening mission rolled up in a truck. I made the snap decision that they weren’t interested in a lengthy conversation, so I skipped the opportunity to defuse the situation and aimed at their knees with both barrels. Although this is a scripted scenario that everyone will face in their opening minutes with GTA 6, it’s emblematic of what could happen at any moment on the streets of Leonida.

Later, while browsing a shoe shop in Chapter 2, I overheard a shifty-looking man talking about me on a phone call, only for a motorcycle to fly through the glass window of the store seconds later, followed by a hail of bullets. This random event turned my quiet search for a new pair of sandals for Lucia into a 20-minute-long car chase involving gang members and the police. I just wanted to buy some shoes.

Back at Key Lento, the next task I chose to complete was heading to the mechanic to fix up my rusted ride. Cars are obviously a huge part of Grand Theft Auto, but more than ever, customising them is part of the lifestyle. After restoring the engine and taking advantage of the Ultimate Edition exclusive retro build — this particular car is only available in Chapter 1, so make the most of it while you can — I headed out to see what the day had in store for me next.

I flicked open the map to see where the next mission was, but got sidetracked by the opportunity to change up Jason’s hairstyle, so headed to the barber first. GTA 6 really isn’t a game you want to rush; it really is true that the more you put into its open world and characters, the more you’ll get out of it in the long run. Plus, a snazzy new trim would surely please Lucia when she sees me upon her imminent release from prison. A small love heart popping up on the right-hand side of the screen confirms this. Little activities here and there consistently build up how strong the couple’s bond is, such as whether you choose to fully patch up Jason’s home so Lucia doesn’t come back to a living room with holes in the roof or steps that could snap at any moment. It makes every decision, small or big, feel impactful over the course of the whole journey, injecting a subtle aspect of choice and consequence into a Rockstar game like never before.

Anyway, after spending far too much on a chevron moustache, I continued going about my business. A man using his boutique as a front for a drugs lab refused to hand over the money he owed Brian, so I was presented with a choice. I quickly sized him up and decided he posed no danger to me, so opted to threaten him rather than defuse the situation. My instincts were correct, as he lifted up a baseball bat from below his desk but quickly gave himself up after I yanked it from him. He then ran away before giving me the code to an office as I took the acid he’d been cooking up as payment. I then drove it to a nearby lockup where I could drop the drugs off for Brian.

This is a simple encounter on the surface, with a single choice at its core, but one that cleverly teaches you how the hundreds of ever-escalating robberies you’ll commit from this point on work. Make the right decision, and you’ll get the info you’ll need to not have to brute force your way into backrooms, safes, and vaults, setting off very loud alarms in the process. If you want to be as professional as possible and pride yourself on clean exits, studying your surroundings and the people within them will be key, especially in some of Vice City’s biggest banks.

And so I made my way to the next mission marker, but not before getting distracted several times along the way. There’s always something aiming to catch your eye or ear in Leonida, whether it be the cops making an arrest by the side of the road, or a bright pink van sat outside a local seafood restaurant with “our shrimp is so pimp” written on the side. It felt rude to not put that claim to the test, so I treated Jason to a crawfish po-boy for lunch. My health bar was now back to full after taking a hit from that earlier ambush; I set off again. But, of course, another distraction was just minutes away.

Strangers and freaks have long been a part of Rockstar’s open worlds, and GTA 6 is absolutely full of them. The one closest to home, literally, is your neighbour Shirley. An older woman sporting unmissable bright blue eyeshadow and holding her pink-ribbon-wearing dog in her hand, she’s living the Leonida life. Further evidence of this is how her front yard has a sun lounger set up on it with a drinks cabinet standing nearby. Shirley loves a drink, but had sadly run out of rum for her Mai Tais. Because I’m such a nice neighbour, I run over to the liquor store for her to collect the bottle, an errand which itself creates a distraction within a distraction. It’s distraction Inception in South Leonida.

When stepping into the store, I watch as the clerk walks in from a back room echoing with the sound of exotic birds. Curiously, when I question him about it, he clearly lies and says it’s the noise of a nature TV show. My map tells me differently, creating a new robbery opportunity icon on it thanks to this new info. A new invitation for a taste of crime has popped up, and I gladly accept it, but not before picking up a pack of chips. Jason impressively opens them and eats the contents with just one hand, his second still gripping the bottle of rum. The animation work is truly astounding, often providing a bespoke solution to any action you can think of attempting.

I carefully store the rum in the back of my car and swap it for my shotgun, my trigger finger itching from not being used in half an hour. There were many ways to approach this operation — stealth was certainly an option — but I felt like letting loose a bit, so I used a dumpster to climb onto the store’s roof, took aim at an explosive gas canister for the fun of it, and then blasted each of the five people that stood in the way of whatever treasures they were hiding. I’ll be transparent with you: this is the third time I’ve played through this encounter over the course of my experiments with GTA 6, and it’s the only occasion I’d actually thought to stop and talk to the bright red parrot chirping away in it. I asked him about the money, and he mentioned a nearby generator. Lo and behold, a vent next to it had roughly $1,500 in cash hidden within – a fortune at this early stage. It’s yet another lesson in taking your time to analyse your environment paying off in this world.

So, I headed back to Shirley, finally gifting her the rum she so desperately requested. It was now 4pm, too late to stay for a chat, so I headed around the corner for my next objective. Another woman greeted me in her yard, and seeing as the mission was called “Pipework”, combined with the flirtatious way she said hello plus the fact that her underwear was peeking over the top of her quite short shorts, I could see where this may be heading. I was there to collect rent for Brian, but in order to get it, I’d need to unblock Mandy’s sink. I just wanted to get in and out, so to speak — I made the decision from minute one of GTA 6 that I’m ride or die with Lucia, and no one could steer me from that path. Mandy, bless her, tried her best, though.

I used a plunger on her sink — again, not a euphemism — and then headed under it to play around with the pipes. Then, in a scene not too dissimilar from the sort the British government really don’t want you watching anymore, Mandy strode into the kitchen wearing a bikini that only barely covered her. I clenched the wrench tighter, twisting the pipe as fast as I could, and began my getaway as she angrily berated me for my lack of interest in her. I wasn’t outright offered the opportunity to cheat on Lucia, but I certainly wasn’t entertaining the notion. I walked out, not before taking an apple for my troubles on the way. Mandy, of course, wished I was eating an entirely different type of fruit.

This is a scenario that reared its head every now and then over my 70-hour playthrough, with other gym-goers, for example, offering their number to Jason. If Lucia finds out you accepted it, she won’t be happy, and all the hard work you did pleasing her with those new steps in your home will have gone to waste. It’s yet another distraction GTA 6 puts your way, and one that I won’t judge you for exploring. Lucia will, though.

Temptation is everywhere in Leonida. Whether it be from its people or the opportunities that throw themselves your way at every turn. It’s an open world that remembers your actions, learns who you are, and rewards patience. Consequences for your choices made on both a micro and macro level are at the very heart of its themes, and committing to role-playing Jason and Lucia as real humans that are part of this world, rather than hurricanes of violence that rip through it, pays off by its story’s end. The first hour or so of stepping into Jason’s shoes teaches you all of this, even if you don’t realise you’re playing through gaming’s most polished tutorial. It’s a near-perfect piece of game design, and just the tip of the iceberg of what's to come.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Forged Resolve Walkthrough - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Forged Resolve is the third main story quest in the Charting the Unknown DLC for Crimson Desert. Oongka heads to Pailune seeking a way to improve his cannon.
articles.body:
Forged Resolve is the third main story quest in the Charting the Unknown DLC for Crimson Desert . Oongka heads to Pailune seeking a way to improve his cannon. This leads to his goal of learning engineering so he can become stronger to protect his friends. This IGN guide covers how to complete all 10 subquests within Forged Resolve. Click the links below to jump straight to our dedicated walkthroughs:

Head to the northwest side of Pailune to start the Forged Resolve questline with A New Path. Your first objective leads to a cutscene where Oongka spends some time researching his cannon inside a workshop. Once the cutscene is over, head a short distance over to Wynstan, near the Rancher.

Talk to Wynstan to ask him if he has anything Oongka can use as a power source for his cannon. Despite Wynstan explaining that he never gets anything that powerful, he encourages Oongka to search elsewhere. Oongka then muses to himself about visiting the Scholastone Institute next. This completes the short quest, A New Path.

To Scholastone sends you to an objective near Kharonso , not far from the Scholastone Institute. In case you need a reminder, this is far south-southwest of Pailune. Upon arriving at the quest marker, you'll find a troll scholar named Grimrick. They're standing near a magical gray pyramid.

Talk to Grimrick to ask how to reach the Scholastone Institute. He'll then offer to guide you there while chatting about a familiar story you may recall. He mentions a previous Greymane visiting Scholastone, who saved them from a disaster. The next cutscene kicks in as you approach a windmill, where Grimrick then looks out at the institute in the distance.

Once the cutscene is over, travel to the Scholastone Institute to complete this quest. It'll finish on its own once you get close or if you use the Abyss Nexus near there.

Now that you've made it to the Scholastone Institute, head inside and find Dean Grundir . After entering the institute from the south side, head past the giant floating globe and through the magical door ahead. This leads to the library where the dean is.

Speak to Dean Grundir to start a cutscene where Oongka inquires about learning engineering. Before sending Oongka away, he sends him to a scholar named Vargus. Fortunately, the cutscene ends near Vargus, so you won't have to track him down.

Speak to Vargus , where Oongka again explains that he wants to learn engineering. Before learning anything, Vargus asks that Oongka repair the lab's Power Regulator. Without explaining why, he prefers that you keep it quiet. Once the cutscene finishes, you'll be in front of the power regulator for a puzzle.

Arriving in front of the Power Regulator, near the Scholastone Archive, it's time to repair this machine during Unfamiliar Workshop. Examine it first and take a look at the inscribed text near the top of the machine. This reveals the following message:

When a position's signal reaches its limit, the calculation carries over to the next position. If the total exceeds the allowed limit, the device may overload.

Input Device No. 5: Damaged. Do not operate.

This inscription tells us almost everything we need to know about the puzzle, but it can be a little confusing to understand. The Base Sequence explains which blocks along the bottom third row need to be lit. Each one represents a lit block, and each zero is for an inactive block. The main challenge comes into play when attempting to light the second column since the blocks there are broken.

The second part of the inscription hints that overloading a column will send its power to the next column (to the left). This is the trick to lighting up that second broken column. Therefore, the solution is visible in the table below, where each 1 represents a block to press. You can also check the image below the table.

Upon solving the puzzle, a new cutscene starts with a montage of Oongka learning engineering. After about four minutes, the cutscene ends and completes two quests: Unfamiliar Workshop and Faltering Hands, Iron Will. You'll also receive the Skyway Rocket Pack for finishing these quests. With that said, you still won't be able to fly unless you've unlocked the Flight skill.

As mentioned in the previous quest section, Faltering Hands, Iron Will, starts and completes during a cutscene. This quest requires no action from the player.

The Fractured Door quest sends you on a journey that you won't be able to immediately return from. Due to this, we recommend stocking up on food and any other preparations you may need to do first . Such as upgrading your gear if you want to.

Once you're ready, head to the index, near the Scholastone Archive. This is where the quest info hints that Vargas may be. While ascending the index stairs, you'll encounter the warning about being restricted to the quest temporarily. Continue past the warning and up the stairs to find a door with a puzzle to open it.

Similar to the earlier puzzle with the Power Regulator, we recommend examining the door first . This will reveal a written inscription above the door with helpful information. It states the following rules:

There's an even harder problem waiting inside.

Before interacting with the door puzzle, you won't see the puzzle quite yet. So try not to confuse yourself by staring at the door before revealing the puzzle part. Upon using the Operate button prompt, you'll see a gridded board with a Control Panel handle at the bottom left corner.

For this puzzle, there's no limit on how many times you can fail, so don't worry about that. As the rules explain, you'll need to flip/highlight the entire board, excluding the walls, within only 15 moves. Each time you move in a direction while holding the Control Panel, you'll move all the way across the board in that direction. This counts as one move.

We've included the Fractured Door puzzle solution via each step below and an image too that may be a little trickier to follow:

The red arrows and blue arrows in the image below for each direction alternate. For example, the first step shows a red arrow going up. The second step shows a blue arrow to the right. And then the third step is back to the red arrow, now going down.

Upon solving the puzzle, Oongka finds Vargas inside. This is where you'll learn that he's restarted Octavius' disastrous research. He explains his goal of using a visione as a transporter to travel via a different realm. However, he needs Oongka's help. This leads to Oongka placing the visione on his head and traveling through the gate.

Before escaping the dark abyss, you'll be greeted by Marni's Butler. After a moment, you'll end up inside Marni's manor, marked on the map as the Museum of Marni. During the cutscene, Oongka wanders around the manor while Marni's Butler rambles on. Once the cutscene is over, the Fractured Door quest is complete.

Fateful Encounter continues from the previous quest now that you're inside Marni's manor. Your first step in an attempt to return to Scholastone is to figure out how to get past the nearby locked iron gate.

If you're not sure where to look for opening this locked iron gate, it can get confusing quickly. Most of the manor is available to look around, when the reality is, you don't have to look far. Search the room near the door to see if anything jumps out at you.

What we're looking for here is the six candles on the wall to the right of it , with an inscription below them. If you look at the inscription and then examine it, you'll get the following message:

Light the tallest candle, and let its neighbors sleep.

Let light and darkness alternate to complete the circle.

These short instructions tell you everything you'll need to know to unlock the gate. From this information, we can deduce that we'll need to light certain candles. The first sentence states to light the tallest candle, referring to the top one. By saying to let its neighbors sleep, we can assume it's referring to the one to the tallest candle's left and right.

After following the first sentence's clue, the second one starts to make more sense. You can now alternate the rest of them to learn which ones need to be lit. The solution is: Tap to Reveal , as shown in the picture below.

Once you've unlocked the iron gate, head through to start a cutscene. This leads to a memory where Marni practically speaks directly to you. He explains that you ended up in his home due to restrictions he put on using the visione to travel. In order to return to Scholastone, you'll need to find the Homecoming Device that he mentions.

After the cutscene ends, Oongka asks the Marni Butler where the device is. While it doesn't tell you where it is, it does escort you on the right path. Follow the Marni Butler outside, around the manor, and then back inside. It'll eventually stop at the top of the stairs to the second floor, near a set of drawers with a book on it. Grab the book, Marni and the Secret Chamber.

You can then follow the butler down the nearby hall to a room at the end. This leads to a short cutscene with the butler rambling some more. If you haven't already, examine the book you recently grabbed, Marni and the Secret Chamber. You'll find it inside your Key inventory category, not the one for books. Reading the book reveals a clue to place it near other books.

Using this clue, you should start searching for other books around the manor that it may fit with. This could be a desk, a set of drawers, or a bookshelf. If you want the answer quickly, Tap to Reveal .

Once you've found the right spot, look at the top of what's mentioned in the spoiler tag. You'll find a button prompt to Plant it there. This leads to a hidden door revealing itself that you can walk through. Enter the secret room and approach the desk inside to start a cutscene. Oongka then finds some plans to use for improving his cannon.

During this cutscene, Marni's butler hints to not touch a crooked picture frame. Unfortunately, it doesn't say where the picture frame is, so you'll have to search around a bit. You can find the crooked picture frame Tap to Reveal .

Examine the crooked Picture Frame to fix it. You should then hear a click sound come from the nearby door to your left. The camera will also focus in on it too. Enter through the now unlocked door to find an ominously empty room. If you're extra observant, you may notice a seam along the floor for a trapdoor. Step on that spot to drop down into a hidden workshop.

Upon falling through the trapdoor, walk forward a little to trigger a cutscene. Marni's butler will appear and explain where you now are. Once the cutscene is finished, Fateful Encounter is complete.

Now that you're in Marni's secret workshop, it's time to work on the blueprint Oongka found. You'll need to gather five different item types that are explained in the table below:

Once you've found all of the necessary materials, return to the table with the giant rotating gears beyond it. This starts an eight-minute cutscene that begins with a montage of Oongka crafting a hand cannon. During the cutscene, you'll find the Homecoming Device, hear more rambling from Marni's butler, and see a couple of changes as Oongka travels different dimensions. Such as the Reed Devil fighting off bandits and T'rukan the Ascended advising the Jijeong Monk as their master.

Oongka eventually floats over to a timeline where the Greymanes were slaughtered. This reveals the Pailune Castle in ruin as Oongka tries to understand the carnage. The cutscene ends with someone calling out to him, which then completes The Scattered Pieces. You'll also receive the Enhanced Fatum Blaster as a reward.

articles.title: Now That I've Played GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, Here's What I Want Out of the PC Version
articles.summary: After playing GTA 6 all day yesterday on everything from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro, I'm forming a clearer picture on what a PC version of the game should look like.
articles.body:
This is an opinion piece by Jackie Thomas, IGN's Senior Tech Editor who's been covering PC games and the components that make them run for more than a decade.

GTA 6 is exclusive to consoles at launch, but everyone knows a PC version will come out eventually. And when it does, it'll probably be the best way to play the game, provided you have the hardware to run it at a high frame rate.

While I know that's a tough bar to clear with prices being what they are these days, after playing GTA 6 all day yesterday on everything from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro , I'm forming a clearer picture on what a PC version of the game should look like.

Obviously, the first thing that the PC version of GTA 6 is going to be able to do that the console version can't is actually hit 60fps. Rockstar itself came out and said that a 60fps patch won't be coming to the PS5 Pro because it's simply not powerful enough. And, well, that wasn't super surprising . The PC version will be able to hit 60fps, but I think it might be a bit of a struggle for a lot of the PCs out there.

Every single current-generation console is housing an AMD Zen 2 CPU with 8 cores and 16 threads, and if we were just going off core counts alone, that would match or exceed the vast majority of gaming PCs out there, according to the Steam Hardware Survey. However, in the six years since Zen 2's debut in the Ryzen 7 2700X, IPC (Instructions per Clock) performance has risen so much that I doubt most recent 8-core CPUs are going to have the same troubles with players blowing shit up in GTA than the consoles have right now.

The problem is, unlike graphics cards , CPUs are often one of the last things people upgrade in their PCs, so I imagine there are still a lot of older 8-core CPUs out there that aren't dramatically faster than what you'd find in the PS5 and Xbox Series X. But if you do have a more recent mid-to-high end CPU like the AMD Ryzen 7000 or 9000 series or anything Intel post 12th-gen, you should be able to push GTA 6 to a higher frame rate than the consoles.

Right now, as I write this, I'm sitting next to a rig with an AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D and an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 , and if the furthest I can push this game is 60fps, I don't even know if it's going to be worth double dipping. The real difference to GTA 6's frame rate on PC probably isn't going to come from the brute force of the hardware, but the software suites. Now, Rockstar did some excellent work with the upscaling solutions available to them, and even used FSR 4.1 to great effect to get the game running as well as it did on the Xbox Series S. But, as good as FSR and PSSR are, they just aren't as good as DLSS.

My hope would be that Rockstar makes full use of Nvidia's software suite to both make for cleaner upscaling and frame generation. I know that frame gen is a controversial technology, but a game like GTA 6 is perfect for it. After all, it's a slower paced single-player open world game that doesn't need you to have lightning-fast reflexes to succeed, so the added latency won't really be a big deal.

I'll probably finish the game at 30fps on the PS5 Pro, and I'm already pretty used to that frame rate, but on PC, I'll be fully expecting to use frame gen to push that number up to 240fps on my monitor, which will make the game much smoother and easier on the eyes.

GTA 6's move to PC is going to be about more than just upping the frame rate though. As good as the game looks on console – and it looks f**king incredible – it's going to look even better on a PC that can push it to its limits. While the PS5 Pro uses ray traced global illumination, reflections and shadows, then pairs it with PSSR for a clean, beautiful image with excellent lighting, there are still some dials Rockstar can turn to bring the game to another level.

Chief among these is going to be path tracing. Back when Cyberpunk 2077 implemented its 'RT Overdrive' preset, it completely changed the way the game looked. Just looking at the PS5 Pro version of GTA 6 as a baseline, path tracing could elevate the game to a point where it's eerily close to photorealism.

Of course, implementing path tracing would have a huge hit to performance, and GTA 6 isn't exactly going to be a walk in the park for most gaming PCs. For the most part though, lighting settings would hammer your graphics card, and the biggest limiting factor for GTA 6 performance on console right now is the CPU, rather than the GPU. Again, it's hard to get metrics to see exactly how hard each processor in the PS5 Pro is being hit by GTA 6, but if the majority of the processing is being done on the CPU, adding more work for the GPU to do while it waits for the CPU probably isn't going to affect performance as much as you'd think.

Word on the street is that the PC version of GTA 6 is going to come sooner than in past generations, so we hopefully won't have to wait long to see what it can do. I personally hope Rockstar uses the PC port as an opportunity to create the ultimate version of the game. Luckily, that's exactly what it did with Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5, even if they both had buggy launches.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Amy Poehler and Mike Schur Reunite for Dig, a Hilarious New Peacock Mystery Series That Overcomes a Slow Start to Become Your Next Binge-Watch
articles.summary: Amy Poehler and Mike Schur reunite for Dig, a new Peacock comedy that takes a while to get going but ultimately unearths a hilarious and thrilling mystery.
articles.body:
Minor spoilers below for Dig, streaming November 23 on Peacock.

Dig is a gem of a TV show, even if it takes a while to pull it from the ground. The new workplace comedy from Amy Poehler and Mike Schur, who previously worked together on the long-running sitcom Parks and Recreation , takes standard issue office hijinx, moves them to a sun-drenched European locale, and weaves in a propulsive mystery that Agatha Christie would be proud of.

Poehler stars as Elise, the prickly but loveable site manager of an archaeological dig site in Greece. Elise spends her days searching for buried antiquities, wrangling a cadre of horny, fumbling students, and keeping tabs on her pompous dinosaur of a boss, played by Hugh Laurie with a sense of comedic melancholy.

When Elise is passed over for a promotion after dig leader Neville (Laurie) decides to stick around for another year, she promptly stumbles upon a one-of-a-kind buried artifact and draws a group of colleagues into a web of secrets and mysteries. It’s a shame it takes a while for the show to get rolling because, once it does, it’s thrilling and hilarious.

All 10 episodes of Dig premiere at once on Peacock. The binge drop is nothing new but, for this show in particular, is a lifesaver. The first few episodes are funny enough, but often drag to the point of being boring. The action starts in medias res, with Elise and three of her colleagues — ditzy Patty (Fina Strazza), prim Clare (Antonia Thomas), and vivacious Dylan (Geraldine Viswanathan) — caught in a slapstick brawl involving biting, punching, someone getting shot in the leg, and a character falling into a giant pit. (What’s up with Mike Schur, Amy Poehler, and people falling into fictional pits?) But when we flash back several weeks to the main timeline of the show, things slow down substantially.

We spend several episodes introducing a wide cast of characters, the myriad ins and outs of archaeology and dig sites, and the various dramatic backstories and relationships of each of our main characters. We find out Dylan left Elise hanging years prior when the two wanted to start their own dig together while Clare is engaged to her perfectly fine colleague Randy (Jon Pointing) but longs for something more. Patty is a naive farm girl seeing the world for the first time. All of this setup is necessary for any show to be truly durable, but the first several episodes of Dig risk forsaking an engaging plot by spending too much time meandering through the characters’ histories.

Halfway through the season, Dig hits the accelerator and doesn’t look back until the finale’s credits cut to black. The buried artifact Elise found — and promptly shared with only a select group of colleagues — is stolen and the show kicks into high gear with double crosses, character development, and farce. The show’s central mystery — Who stole the artifact and where is it? — allows the writers to throw their characters in numerous, high-pressure situations (Infiltrating a fancy party! A walk of shame in front of a hook-up’s scolding mother! A road full of sheep!) that both propel the plot forward and dig deeper into what makes those characters tick.

As Elise, Poehler plays against type as a weary, often grumpy midlevel site manager. She still serves plenty of one-liners and uses her immense acting chops and top-tier timing to weave together the show’s comedic and dramatic elements. It’s miles away from the sunny, hyper-driven Leslie Knope, but it’s still a marvelous performance. It can be jarring to see Poehler, known for her laugh-out-loud performances across movies and TV, play what amounts to the straight man here, but she translates Elise’s frustrations, longing for the top job, and drive into a fully drawn character.

Poehler’s zag allows for three of her main co-stars to alternate driving the show’s more laugh-out-loud moments. As Dylan, Viswanathan takes the role that Poehler would have played 20 years ago: a bawdy party girl who came back to the dig to get back at her ex-boyfriend and wears ballcaps with crude language while dining out. Thomas’s Clare is a counterweight: proper, intelligent, and striving to prove to her rich, controlling mother that she can be her own woman. Which brings us to Patty.

As the naive, cornfed graduate assistant who’s brand new to the dig site, Fina Strazza’s breakout character is both endearing and lights-out hilarious. From delivering ditzy one-liners to playing a scene against a talking scorpion to runs of incredible physical comedy (there’s a bit with a water bottle and a tube of sunscreen that I can’t get out of my head), Strazza propels what could be a one-dimensional character into a scene-stealing performance.

Once they establish their relationship dynamics, Poehler, Viswanathan, Thomas, and Strazza are unstoppable together. They create a solid core of characters with shifting loyalties that the writers constantly pick apart and reshuffle to great effect.

The cast is rounded out by a who’s who of Schur-verse standbys. Jason Mantzoukas shows up as a dig site looter. Mo Collins is hilarious as someone Patty meets in a hot tub. Rashida Jones even cameos. It’s a palette Schur has played with before to great effect in shows like Parks and Recreation, The Good Place, and a stint on the American version of The Office. But what Dig has that those shows don’t is a sense of adventure and genre inventiveness.

The sun-drenched Grecian locale (which, let’s face it, is obviously a CGI’d Southern California for the most part) is almost irrelevant, which is odd to consider given the show’s reliance on archaeology and history as its central theme. While the distinct outdoor nature of the show does make it stand out against more standard sitcom fare, the skill with which the cast and creators of Dig eventually blend both comedy and thrills would make it a must-watch show if it was set in a strip mall parking lot.

It’s also nice to have a show like Dig be unafraid of actually moving the story along. Once the plot gets going, storylines are deftly planted, executed, and resolved. There are no drawn-out will-they-won’t-they relationships. Characters are free to be multidimensional with motivations rooted in moral gray areas. Poehler herself drops more f-bombs throughout the season than you’d ever have expected.

It all amounts to a show that’s both familiar and inventive. The pop culture references, puns, and sarcastic asides that are foundational to every Mike Schur sitcom are still there. A motley cast of characters gets themselves into more jams than you can possibly count. Characters pair off in scene after scene, creating in-universe in-jokes that circle back episodes later. But Dig also takes the classic half-hour TV comedy and breathes some life into the format by inserting some great thrills and mystery. While it takes way too long to kick into gear, I’m hopeful that the back half of Dig’s first batch of episodes portends a full-throttle Season 2.

articles.title: Paramount+ Plans Drop to $2.99/Month for Black Friday
articles.summary: All Paramount+ plans have dropped to $2.99/month for your first two months, including the ad-free premium plan that comes with Showtime.
articles.body:
Paramount+ has announced the details of its 2026 Black Friday deal, now live through November 30.

The deal is pretty much the same as last year. All Paramount+ plans have dropped to $2.99/month for your first two months, including the ad-free premium plan that comes with Showtime.

This is the first major streaming deal to go live for Black Friday , but it will likely be one of the only ad-free discounts we see all year.

Paramount+ currently offers two different plans . Paramount+ Essential, which normally costs $8.99/month, offers the standard Paramount+ library with ads. Paramount+ Premium ups the monthly cost to $13.99, removing ads and getting you the additional Showtime library.

The Black Friday deal drops both plans to $2.99 for your first two months. The discount is available to both new and eligible returning subscribers, so if you’re already paying the standard monthly fee, you’ll have to do a little cancellation magic or make a new account to get in on the deal. I leave that up to you.

The only reason to go with the cheaper plan is if you’re particularly nervous about remembering to cancel before it auto-renews. In terms of savings, you save 67% with the Essential deal compared to almost 80% off with Premium. You’ll get the added benefit of shows like Yellowjackets, and, of course, you won’t have to deal with ads.

Two months isn’t a particularly long window, but it’s pretty standard for the larger Paramount+ deals. It’s more than enough time to watch all of Avatar: Seven Havens , catch up on South Park , or pay tribute to Patrick Stewart with some Star Trek .

The short window is even less surprising in 2026. Paramount recently completed its acquisition of Warner Bros., and plans to launch a new bundle with HBO Max in the new year. The company is likely angling for new subscribers who, after the two-month Black Friday deal ends, would be ready to sign onto the new bundle.

HBO Max hasn’t revealed their own Black Friday deal yet, but we’ll likely see a similar 'limited' subscription window attached to it.

More Black Friday Streaming Deals Are on the Way

We’re hurdling toward Black Friday, and while most of the minds at IGN are on the mammoth that is GTA 6 , I’m keeping an eye out for all of the streaming deals. Last year, we got full deals from pretty much every service except Peacock, and I’m expecting pretty similar discounts to return over the next week.

articles.title: Games - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are four types of video and arcade games you can play in Grand Theft Auto VI. All games can be played at home on your console after completing the
articles.body:
There are four types of video and arcade games you can play in Grand Theft Auto VI . All games can be played at home on your console after completing the Chapter 1 mission Tap to Reveal , but Bang For Your Buck and Street Trash 3: Dezombifier can also be played at arcades around Leonida. In this official IGN GTA 6 guide, you'll find an overview of all the video and arcade games you can play in your downtime, and the specific challenges they offer to test your skills.

If you want to achieve 100% progress in the game, you'll need to complete the four following games. These range from top-down shooters, to first-person shooters, and puzzle games.

Bang For Your Buck is a first-person shooter, where you'll need to hunt animals as fast as you can. As the timer ticks down, you'll lose money, so you need to keep killing to keep earning. For every kill you get, you'll earn cash, and there are additional boxes you can hit to boost your bucks quicker.

There are five challenges to complete while playing through Bang For Your Buck. However, other achievements are also tracked including your A++ Grades, Stages Completed, Trophies Killed, Shotgun Kills, and more.

This top-down shooter sees you take on a zombie outbreak that's destroying Freedom City. You'll need to extract by collecting six gears, which randomly spawn across the maps. You'll need to watch your health, continuously shoot at zombies, and consider your stamina as you dodge them to try to survive. Perk Cards can also be unlocked, which give you buffs including additinal XP from kills, health regeneration, increased rate of fire, and more.

Tenebrae Lux is an indie walking simulator and puzzle game, where you'll wash up on an island and be tasked with making your way toward the lighthouse. As you explore the island, there's documents for you to find and puzzles to solve, to uncover the mystery of the island.

Time Jackers: Rewind is a top-down, twin-stick shooter that takes place in 2084. You'll have a limited amount of time to complete the game, as you try to take down the DominiCorp.

articles.title: DC Reveals First Details About Absolute Justice, the First Absolute Universe Crossover
articles.summary: DC has revealed exciting new details about Absolute Justice, the epic 2027 crossover that pits Batman and his allies against the Justice League.
articles.body:
DC's Absolute Universe line is a huge hit, but outside of a brief Absolute Batman/Absolute Wonder Woman crossover, we've yet to see the heroes of this bleak world join forces. That's finally set to change in early 2027 as DC kicks off Absolute Justice.

Absolute Justice is a five-issue limited series that brings together Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, Flash, Green Lantern, and Martian Manhunter. These six heroes will be forced to unite against the Justice League , which in this world consists of billionaires and oligarchs like Ra's al Ghul, Veronica Cale, Hector Hammond, Dr. Elenore Thawne, Lex Luthor, and Jack Grimm (aka The Joker). DC promises that the series will be completely standalone, "with no tie-in issues, no crossovers, and no mercy shown!"

Absolute Justice is written by Absolute Superman's Jason Aaron, with art by Juan Ferreyra (who drew the latter half of Aaron's TMNT run). The first issue features a host of covers, including a main cover by Ferreyra and variants by Stanley “Artgerm” Lau, Gabriele Dell’Otto, Rafael Albuquerque, and Kyuyong Eom. Issue #1 will also be available as a $9.99 blind bag variant, with exclusive covers by Jim Lee, Kaare Andrews, Mark Brooks, Dan Mora, and Álvaro Martínez Bueno.

Here's DC's official summary of Absolute Evil #1:

The Absolute Universe was born in the image of Darkseid, but the emergence of its heroes has introduced something its creator never intended: hope. The billionaires and industrialists who rule this world see that rising hope as a dangerous infection that must be eradicated.

Those rulers have a name: the Justice League.

In Absolute Justice, the Justice League will call upon Darkseid, and Darkseid will send his angels with a message for the heroes of this world: Abandon all hope.

In the face of a threat that seeks to undo everything they’ve accomplished, the solitary heroes of the Absolute Universe must unite for the very first time and go to war against the forces of creation itself! From the blockbuster creative team of Jason Aaron and Juan Ferreyra comes an event series that will change the Absolute Universe forever…with no tie-in issues, no crossovers, and no mercy shown!

Absolute Evil #1 will be released on April 7, 2027. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

articles.title: Downing Street Hails GTA 6 as 'British Success Story' — But UK PM Andy Burnham Is Too Busy to Play
articles.summary: Downing Street says UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham won't be playing GTA 6 due to a "very full" diary, while hailing the game as a British success story.
articles.body:
Downing Street says U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham won't be playing GTA 6 due to a "very full" diary, while hailing the game as a British success story.

While Rockstar's masterpiece is now available worldwide with millions of players getting started, one notable Brit isn't calling in sick with GTA flu. According to a spokesperson for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the PM is simply too busy to sit down and escape to sunny Leonida.

Still, No 10 happily claimed the blockbuster release as a "British success story," owing to its creation by Rockstar North in Edinburgh, even if various other Rockstar studios worldwide contributed.

"Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh, and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait," a No 10 spokesperson said, as reported by The Independent . When asked whether the PM himself would be venturing into Vice City, however, the spokesperson stated: "His diary is very full. He won’t be playing it."

No one else should be pulling a "GTA sickie," either, the spokesperson continued — and younger fans in particular "should be in classrooms today and tomorrow," because "every day in school matters."

This week, "GTA flu" trended online as countless staff called in sick , with businesses fearing a measurable hit to production in some countries. Schools have also been warning children not to skip classes in order to stay home and play GTA 6, with some pupils even being offered gift cards as an incentive to actually show up .
